sections.leaf: Alternate, simple, entire but may have a few shallow lobes at tip, elliptical to oblong-obovate, leathery and nearly evergreen, edges may be rolled, 1 to 3 inches long, 1/2 to 1 inch wide, shiny dark green above, paler below.
sections.flower: Species is monoecious; male flowers are yellow-green long catkins (1 1/2 to 3 inches long), females are green to reddish, very small spike in leaf axils, appearing with the leaves.
sections.fruit: Small acorn (1/2 inch or less), nut round, brown with some fuzz, cap is shallow covering 1/4 of nut.
sections.twig: Slender, light brown to gray, hairless; buds are sharp pointed reddish brown and clustered at twig ends.
sections.bark: Initially smooth, and gray-brown, later splitting into fissures and flat ridges and becoming darker.
sections.form: Medium size tree to 60 feet, 1 to 3 feet in diameter, usually smaller with a rounded crown.
sections.looks_like: laurel oak - shingle oak - bluejack oak - willow oak

sections.habit: Trees , evergreen or tardily deciduous, to 35 m.
sections.bark: much like that of Q . laurifolia .
sections.twigs: light brown to dark red-brown, 1-2.5 mm diam., glabrous.
sections.terminal_buds: reddish to purplish brown, ovoid, 2.5-5 mm, glabrous or with ciliate scale margins.
sections.leaf_blade: narrowly ovate or elliptic to oblanceolate, 30-120 × 10-40 mm, leathery, base obtuse to rounded, rarely attenuate, margins entire or with a few shallow lobes or teeth near apex, awns 1-4 (rarely as many as 8-10 on 2d-flush growth), apex acute or acuminate, occasionally obtuse; surfaces abaxially glabrous, rarely with minute axillary tufts of tomentum, adaxially glabrous.
sections.acorns: biennial; cup saucer-shaped to bowl-shaped, rarely turbinate, 3-10 mm high × 11-18 mm wide, covering 1/4-1/3 nut, outer surface puberulent, inner surface pubescent at least 1/2 distance to rim, scales occasionally distinctly tuberculate, tips appressed, acute to obtuse; nut broadly ovoid to hemispheric, 9-16 × 9-16 mm, glabrate, scar diam. 6-9.5 mm.

sources.distribution: Flowering spring. Moderately dry sandy soils, scrub sandhills, stream banks, occasionally on hillsides and ravines; 0-150 m; Ala., Ark., Fla., Ga., La., Miss., N.C., S.C., Tex., Va.
